bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- People-dependent delivery model exposed to attrition and wage/skill inflation — The BRSR reports a workforce of 237,098 (227,181 permanent) and voluntary attrition (LTM - IT Services) of 12.51% for permanent employees in FY26 against 12.99% in FY25 and 12.42% in FY24. HCLTech owns no plants or manufacturing facilities, so capacity is entirely people; sustained double-digit churn in a business selling billable skills is a structural cost and delivery-continuity risk, aggravated by the need to re-skill the base for AI, automation, cybersecurity and cloud.
- Revenue concentrated in a single business activity and one dominant segment — 100% of turnover comes from one activity - computer programming, consultancy, software and related activities (GICS Information Technology - Software and Services). Within that, IT & Business Services contributes 74% of turnover, Engineering and R&D Services 17% and HCLSoftware 9%. There is no diversifying business line, so any downturn in enterprise IT services demand or in the ITBS segment flows almost fully to the top line.
- Export and currency concentration - over nine-tenths of standalone turnover is exported — The BRSR states exports contribute 91.54% of total turnover for the standalone entity, with markets across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. Revenue is therefore earned largely in foreign currency against a substantially INR/offshore cost base, exposing reported earnings to exchange-rate movement and to demand, immigration and trade policy in a small number of overseas markets.
- Client concentration in a narrow set of very large enterprise accounts — The Company positions itself as a preferred digital and AI partner to Global 2000 companies, Global 2000 equivalent organizations and emerging enterprises, and states that its strategy 'emphasizes building deep, strategic client relationships as a trusted long-term partner'. That deep-few model concentrates revenue in large accounts, so the loss, insourcing or budget cut of a top relationship is disproportionately material.
- Exposure to heavily regulated client verticals and their compliance regimes — Clients are concentrated in Financial Services, Manufacturing, Life Sciences and Healthcare, Technology and Services, Public Services (Energy & Utilities, Travel-Transport-Logistics and Government), Retail and CPG, and Telecommunications, Media, Publishing and Entertainment. Serving regulated and government customers imports their data-protection, security and procurement obligations into HCLTech's delivery, raising the cost of failure on any engagement.
- Sprawling multi-jurisdiction legal-entity structure — As on March 31, 2026 the Company had 125 subsidiaries and 3 associate companies, with new entities incorporated in Austria (HCL Technologies Holdings GmbH) and the UAE (HCL Technologies Middle East LLC) during the year. The Directors' Report acknowledges the burden directly, noting that restructuring is done 'after taking into consideration the business aspects, local laws and regulations' in order to reduce the number of entities - i.e. a standing compliance, tax and administrative-cost overhead across many jurisdictions.
- Acquisition, integration and portfolio-churn execution risk — FY26 saw two acquisitions (Wobby BV, an Agentic AI software startup in Belgium, via Actian Germany GmbH; and Finergic Solutions Pte. Ltd. of Singapore, core banking and wealth-management transformation, via HCL Singapore Pte Ltd, completed March 6, 2026, pulling in Finergic Consulting Pte. Ltd. and Finergic Luxembourg S.A.) alongside five entities merged, liquidated or de-registered - including the liquidation of the CeleritiFinTech Limited joint venture on October 28, 2025. Continuous inorganic capability-buying and entity unwinding carries integration, retention and value-realisation risk.
- Reliance on the internal control, ethics and risk-policy framework rather than a disclosed enterprise risk register — Risk oversight rests on a Board Risk Management Committee (one of six Board Committees), a Risk Management Policy 'that ensures appropriate management of risks in line with its internal systems and culture', and internal financial controls designed for 'safeguarding of assets from unauthorized use & prevention and detection of frauds & errors'. The Directors' Report itself carries no risk enumeration - it defers the detailed Risk Management section to the MD&A - so investors depend on the effectiveness of that framework, and on the auditors' clean report and no-fraud statement, for assurance.

outlook.title: Strategy

outlook.body: HCLTech is asset-light - it does not produce physical products or own/operate any manufacturing facilities - and the routed sections disclose no plant, capacity or rupee capex programme. FY 2025-26 expansion was capability-, footprint- and entity-led. Capability build-out centres on the AI portfolio: AI Factory, described as comprehensive cognitive infrastructure spanning AI data center design, build and operate services; AI Engineering covering Physical AI (embedding intelligence into physical systems and environments) and Kinetic AI (robotics and automation); AI Advisory; and Sovereign AI for governments and heavily regulated sectors that want AI developed, deployed and governed on infrastructure, data and models controlled entirely within their firms. The flagship AI Force platform is now deployed across 75 clients, VisionX addresses multimodal AI for physical operations, and internal deployments include LUMI and Talent Navigator; capacity for this build-out was created by training over 144,000 employees in GenAI in FY26, including 11,800 certified AI Builders and more than 700 certified blackbelts. Footprint expansion came through two new step-down wholly owned subsidiaries - HCL Technologies Holdings GmbH under the laws of Austria and HCL Technologies Middle East LLC under the laws of the UAE - on top of a delivery network already spanning 60 countries. Inorganically, Actian Germany GmbH acquired Wobby BV of Belgium, an Agentic AI software startup providing AI Data Analyst 'Agents' for data warehouses, and HCL Singapore Pte Ltd acquired Finergic Solutions Pte. Ltd. of Singapore, which provides core banking and wealth management transformation programs; completion on March 6, 2026 also brought Finergic Consulting Pte. Ltd. (Singapore) and Finergic Luxembourg S.A. (Luxembourg) in as step-down wholly owned subsidiaries. Running the other way, the Company pursued deliberate entity rationalisation to optimise resources and manage costs, merging or closing five entities during the year - Zeenea Benelux voluntarily liquidated on April 10, 2025; Geometric China, Inc. de-registered on September 24, 2025; the CeleritiFinTech Limited joint venture liquidated on October 28, 2025; Actian International Inc. merged into Actian Corporation on December 1, 2025; and Confinale (UK) Limited voluntarily dissolved on January 27, 2026. On funding, HCL America Inc. fully repaid the balance outstanding USD 252.207 million of 1.375% senior unsecured notes on March 10, 2026, after which the Trustee released the Company's guarantee and no Notes remain outstanding. The Board recorded no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position of the Company between the end of the financial year and the date of the Report.

drhp.expansion: HCLTech is asset-light - it does not produce physical products or own/operate any manufacturing facilities - and the routed sections disclose no plant, capacity or rupee capex programme. FY 2025-26 expansion was capability-, footprint- and entity-led. Capability build-out centres on the AI portfolio: AI Factory, described as comprehensive cognitive infrastructure spanning AI data center design, build and operate services; AI Engineering covering Physical AI (embedding intelligence into physical systems and environments) and Kinetic AI (robotics and automation); AI Advisory; and Sovereign AI for governments and heavily regulated sectors that want AI developed, deployed and governed on infrastructure, data and models controlled entirely within their firms. The flagship AI Force platform is now deployed across 75 clients, VisionX addresses multimodal AI for physical operations, and internal deployments include LUMI and Talent Navigator; capacity for this build-out was created by training over 144,000 employees in GenAI in FY26, including 11,800 certified AI Builders and more than 700 certified blackbelts. Footprint expansion came through two new step-down wholly owned subsidiaries - HCL Technologies Holdings GmbH under the laws of Austria and HCL Technologies Middle East LLC under the laws of the UAE - on top of a delivery network already spanning 60 countries. Inorganically, Actian Germany GmbH acquired Wobby BV of Belgium, an Agentic AI software startup providing AI Data Analyst 'Agents' for data warehouses, and HCL Singapore Pte Ltd acquired Finergic Solutions Pte. Ltd. of Singapore, which provides core banking and wealth management transformation programs; completion on March 6, 2026 also brought Finergic Consulting Pte. Ltd. (Singapore) and Finergic Luxembourg S.A. (Luxembourg) in as step-down wholly owned subsidiaries. Running the other way, the Company pursued deliberate entity rationalisation to optimise resources and manage costs, merging or closing five entities during the year - Zeenea Benelux voluntarily liquidated on April 10, 2025; Geometric China, Inc. de-registered on September 24, 2025; the CeleritiFinTech Limited joint venture liquidated on October 28, 2025; Actian International Inc. merged into Actian Corporation on December 1, 2025; and Confinale (UK) Limited voluntarily dissolved on January 27, 2026. On funding, HCL America Inc. fully repaid the balance outstanding USD 252.207 million of 1.375% senior unsecured notes on March 10, 2026, after which the Trustee released the Company's guarantee and no Notes remain outstanding. The Board recorded no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position of the Company between the end of the financial year and the date of the Report.

risks.note: The BRSR reports a workforce of 237,098 (227,181 permanent) and voluntary attrition (LTM - IT Services) of 12.51% for permanent employees in FY26 against 12.99% in FY25 and 12.42% in FY24. HCLTech owns no plants or manufacturing facilities, so capacity is entirely people; sustained double-digit churn in a business selling billable skills is a structural cost and delivery-continuity risk, aggravated by the need to re-skill the base for AI, automation, cybersecurity and cloud.
risks.risk: People-dependent delivery model exposed to attrition and wage/skill inflation

risks.note: 100% of turnover comes from one activity - computer programming, consultancy, software and related activities (GICS Information Technology - Software and Services). Within that, IT & Business Services contributes 74% of turnover, Engineering and R&D Services 17% and HCLSoftware 9%. There is no diversifying business line, so any downturn in enterprise IT services demand or in the ITBS segment flows almost fully to the top line.
risks.risk: Revenue concentrated in a single business activity and one dominant segment

risks.note: The BRSR states exports contribute 91.54% of total turnover for the standalone entity, with markets across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. Revenue is therefore earned largely in foreign currency against a substantially INR/offshore cost base, exposing reported earnings to exchange-rate movement and to demand, immigration and trade policy in a small number of overseas markets.
risks.risk: Export and currency concentration - over nine-tenths of standalone turnover is exported

risks.note: The Company positions itself as a preferred digital and AI partner to Global 2000 companies, Global 2000 equivalent organizations and emerging enterprises, and states that its strategy 'emphasizes building deep, strategic client relationships as a trusted long-term partner'. That deep-few model concentrates revenue in large accounts, so the loss, insourcing or budget cut of a top relationship is disproportionately material.
risks.risk: Client concentration in a narrow set of very large enterprise accounts

risks.note: Clients are concentrated in Financial Services, Manufacturing, Life Sciences and Healthcare, Technology and Services, Public Services (Energy & Utilities, Travel-Transport-Logistics and Government), Retail and CPG, and Telecommunications, Media, Publishing and Entertainment. Serving regulated and government customers imports their data-protection, security and procurement obligations into HCLTech's delivery, raising the cost of failure on any engagement.
risks.risk: Exposure to heavily regulated client verticals and their compliance regimes

risks.note: As on March 31, 2026 the Company had 125 subsidiaries and 3 associate companies, with new entities incorporated in Austria (HCL Technologies Holdings GmbH) and the UAE (HCL Technologies Middle East LLC) during the year. The Directors' Report acknowledges the burden directly, noting that restructuring is done 'after taking into consideration the business aspects, local laws and regulations' in order to reduce the number of entities - i.e. a standing compliance, tax and administrative-cost overhead across many jurisdictions.

FY26 saw two acquisitions (Wobby BV, an Agentic AI software startup in Belgium, via Actian Germany GmbH; and Finergic Solutions Pte. Ltd. of Singapore, core banking and wealth-management transformation, via HCL Singapore Pte Ltd, completed March 6, 2026, pulling in Finergic Consulting Pte. Ltd. and Finergic Luxembourg S.A.) alongside five entities merged, liquidated or de-registered - including the liquidation of the CeleritiFinTech Limited joint venture on October 28, 2025. Continuous inorganic capability-buying and entity unwinding carries integration, retention and value-realisation risk.
risks.risk: Acquisition, integration and portfolio-churn execution risk

risks.note: Risk oversight rests on a Board Risk Management Committee (one of six Board Committees), a Risk Management Policy 'that ensures appropriate management of risks in line with its internal systems and culture', and internal financial controls designed for 'safeguarding of assets from unauthorized use & prevention and detection of frauds & errors'. The Directors' Report itself carries no risk enumeration - it defers the detailed Risk Management section to the MD&A - so investors depend on the effectiveness of that framework, and on the auditors' clean report and no-fraud statement, for assurance.
risks.risk: Reliance on the internal control, ethics and risk-policy framework rather than a disclosed enterprise risk register

risks.risk: People-dependent delivery model exposed to attrition and wage/skill inflation
risks.note: The BRSR reports a workforce of 237,098 (227,181 permanent) and voluntary attrition (LTM - IT Services) of 12.51% for permanent employees in FY26 against 12.99% in FY25 and 12.42% in FY24. HCLTech owns no plants or manufacturing facilities, so capacity is entirely people; sustained double-digit churn in a business selling billable skills is a structural cost and delivery-continuity risk, aggravated by the need to re-skill the base for AI, automation, cybersecurity and cloud.

risks.risk: Revenue concentrated in a single business activity and one dominant segment
risks.note: 100% of turnover comes from one activity - computer programming, consultancy, software and related activities (GICS Information Technology - Software and Services). Within that, IT & Business Services contributes 74% of turnover, Engineering and R&D Services 17% and HCLSoftware 9%. There is no diversifying business line, so any downturn in enterprise IT services demand or in the ITBS segment flows almost fully to the top line.

risks.risk: Export and currency concentration - over nine-tenths of standalone turnover is exported
risks.note: The BRSR states exports contribute 91.54% of total turnover for the standalone entity, with markets across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. Revenue is therefore earned largely in foreign currency against a substantially INR/offshore cost base, exposing reported earnings to exchange-rate movement and to demand, immigration and trade policy in a small number of overseas markets.

risks.risk: Client concentration in a narrow set of very large enterprise accounts
risks.note: The Company positions itself as a preferred digital and AI partner to Global 2000 companies, Global 2000 equivalent organizations and emerging enterprises, and states that its strategy 'emphasizes building deep, strategic client relationships as a trusted long-term partner'. That deep-few model concentrates revenue in large accounts, so the loss, insourcing or budget cut of a top relationship is disproportionately material.

risks.risk: Exposure to heavily regulated client verticals and their compliance regimes
risks.note: Clients are concentrated in Financial Services, Manufacturing, Life Sciences and Healthcare, Technology and Services, Public Services (Energy & Utilities, Travel-Transport-Logistics and Government), Retail and CPG, and Telecommunications, Media, Publishing and Entertainment. Serving regulated and government customers imports their data-protection, security and procurement obligations into HCLTech's delivery, raising the cost of failure on any engagement.

As on March 31, 2026 the Company had 125 subsidiaries and 3 associate companies, with new entities incorporated in Austria (HCL Technologies Holdings GmbH) and the UAE (HCL Technologies Middle East LLC) during the year. The Directors' Report acknowledges the burden directly, noting that restructuring is done 'after taking into consideration the business aspects, local laws and regulations' in order to reduce the number of entities - i.e. a standing compliance, tax and administrative-cost overhead across many jurisdictions.

risks.risk: Acquisition, integration and portfolio-churn execution risk
risks.note: FY26 saw two acquisitions (Wobby BV, an Agentic AI software startup in Belgium, via Actian Germany GmbH; and Finergic Solutions Pte. Ltd. of Singapore, core banking and wealth-management transformation, via HCL Singapore Pte Ltd, completed March 6, 2026, pulling in Finergic Consulting Pte. Ltd. and Finergic Luxembourg S.A.) alongside five entities merged, liquidated or de-registered - including the liquidation of the CeleritiFinTech Limited joint venture on October 28, 2025. risks.risk: Reliance on the internal control, ethics and risk-policy framework rather than a disclosed enterprise risk register
risks.note: Risk oversight rests on a Board Risk Management Committee (one of six Board Committees), a Risk Management Policy 'that ensures appropriate management of risks in line with its internal systems and culture', and internal financial controls designed for 'safeguarding of assets from unauthorized use & prevention and detection of frauds & errors'. The Directors' Report itself carries no risk enumeration - it defers the detailed Risk Management section to the MD&A - so investors depend on the effectiveness of that framework, and on the auditors' clean report and no-fraud statement, for assurance.

strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.body:
- Become the world's best AI solutions provider - doubling down with conviction on a full-stack AI portfolio built alongside the services offerings, leveraging core engineering DNA and early intellectual-property investments through HCLSoftware.
- Build and scale the Advanced AI category - a self-defined revenue category spanning AI Factory, Physical AI, Robotics, AI Engineering and Custom Silicon, distinct from Classical AI and from the use of AI in traditional services.
- Pursue the opportunity AI creates while absorbing the disruption it brings - offsetting AI-led deflation in traditional services with new AI-led revenue streams.
- Transform HCLTech into an AI-native organization by upskilling people, energized by a growing base of Gen Z talent, on the view that AI multiplies employee capability rather than replaces it.
- Maintain a high-payout shareholder-return philosophy - 97.6% of net income distributed as dividend in FY26, described as one of the highest yields in the industry.
- Drive organisational efficiency by optimising resources and managing costs across countries, integrating businesses amongst subsidiaries through internal restructuring so as to reduce the number of legal entities.
- Add capability inorganically through targeted tuck-ins - Wobby BV (Agentic AI 'Agents' for data warehouses, acquired by Actian Germany GmbH) and Finergic Solutions Pte. Ltd. (core banking and wealth management transformation, acquired by HCL Singapore Pte Ltd).
- Hold governance, employee welfare and board diversity as core - among the highest investors in employee welfare in the industry and one of the most gender-diverse boards in India with over 50% women directors.
- Sustain sustainability leadership - 2030 Scope 1 and Scope 2 reduction targets met four years ahead of schedule and water replenishment at 51 times consumption across operations.
- The Company's wealth distribution philosophy aims at sharing its prosperity with shareholders through a formal earmarking/disbursement of profits, and in accordance with Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations it has formulated and adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy setting out the circumstances under which members may or may not expect dividend, the financial parameters, internal and external factors and the utilisation of retained earnings. Distribution is effected through interim dividends declared during the year - no final dividend was recommended by the Board for FY 2025-26 and there is no book closure for the AGM. The Company has neither any outstanding deposits nor has it accepted deposits from the public, and unclaimed dividends together with the related shares are transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund as required by law. Governance philosophy reinforces this with a stated preference for a simple and transparent corporate structure driven solely by business needs and a clear distinction between personal convenience and corporate resources; CSR spend is governed by a Board-approved CSR Policy and annual action plan overseen by the CSR Committee.

themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
